intro_content:
Getting your finances in order before you arrive on campus is essential. Our online cost estimator can help you estimate your costs and start budgeting for your first year at UBC.

Using your budget as a guide, input your fixed and variable expenses, and the calculator will automatically generate your program’s tuition costs to give you an estimate for your first year.

Each time you update your figures, you’ll get a new estimate. All fees and costs are current estimates based on a first-year full course load.
step1_content: Tell us a bit about you and your study plans at UBC.

educational_costs.title: Here are your educational costs for year one based on your citizenship, campus, and program selections.

tuition.label: Tuition
tuition.description: Based on a full 30-credit course load for the academic year.

student_fees.label: Student fees
student_fees.description: Includes U-Pass, basic health insurance, and more.

lab_clinic_fees.label: Lab or clinic fees
lab_clinic_fees.description: Includes all lab or clinic fees applicable to your selected program.

books_supplies.label: Books and supplies
books_supplies.description: Includes textbooks and other course materials required for your program.

housing.select_housing_label: Where will you live during the school year?

step2_content: Now that you’ve seen your program and school-related costs, it’s time to think about what everyday life will cost. Add your best estimates for things like housing, groceries, and transportation. Enter all values in Canadian dollars (CAD).

housing_expenses.title: Housing
housing_expenses.on_campus_description: We've filled this in based on your choice to live on campus in step one. Learn more about your housing options.
housing_expenses.rent_description: Estimated based on renting a one-bedroom apartment by yourself off-campus in the city. Rent amounts are from Rentals.ca's monthly Rent Report for one-bedroom rentals. If this number isn't right for you, go ahead and change it. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
housing_expenses.rent_description_home: If you will pay rent while living at home, take that into account. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
housing_expenses.utilities_description: Bills like electricity, water, and heating—usually paid monthly if you rent off campus. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
housing_expenses.utilities_description_home: If you will contribute to bills like electricity, water, and heating while living at home, take that into account. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
housing_expenses.move_in_costs_description: One-time purchases like a bureau for your clothes, a lamp, a desk, and even kitchen supplies. Enter the total amount you expect to spend.

food_essentials.title: Food and essentials
food_essentials.meal_plan_description: Prepaid on-campus dining plan based on your earlier selection.
food_essentials.groceries_description: Monthly food shopping in addition to your meal plan—snacks, drinks, and pantry staples. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
food_essentials.groceries_description_prefilled: Estimated monthly food shopping costs. To get an idea of what grocery items cost, see Statistics Canada's report on average retail prices for selected products. If this number isn't right for you, go ahead and change it. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
food_essentials.groceries_description_home: Monthly food shopping—snacks, meals, drinks, and pantry staples. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
food_essentials.toiletries_description: Essentials such as shampoo, toilet paper, and cleaning supplies. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.

transportation.title: Transportation
transportation.transit_description: Access to public transit with a U-Pass is already included in your student fees.
transportation.vehicle_insurance_description: If you drive, include your monthly vehicle insurance costs. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
transportation.gas_parking_maintenance_description: Costs for fuel, parking permits, and occasional car maintenance. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
transportation.car_share_label: Car share membership and usage fees
transportation.car_share_description: If you plan to use a car share service like Evo or Modo, include your monthly membership and typical trip costs. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.

step3_content: Budgeting isn’t just about rent and groceries—add what supports your health, hobbies, and downtime. Enter all values in Canadian dollars (CAD).

health_wellness.title: Health and wellness
health_wellness.extended_health_insurance_description: Monthly expense for any extended health or dental insurance not already included in student fees. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
health_wellness.prescriptions_medical_services_descripti: Medications, doctor visits, dental care, or physiotherapy, for example, not covered by insurance. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
health_wellness.fitness_description: Fitness centre memberships or drop-in classes such as yoga or spin. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.

technology.title: Technology
technology.hardware_description: One-time expense for required tech—like a new phone, laptop, or accessories.  Enter the total amount you expect to spend.
technology.monthly_services_label: Monthly services (internet, cell phone, cable, subscription services)
technology.monthly_services_description: Your monthly phone bill, internet, and any subscriptions like Netflix or Spotify. Enter the total amount you expect to spend each month.

personal_social.title: Personal and social
personal_social.clothing_haircuts_description: Clothing, shoes, personal grooming, and haircuts. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
personal_social.social_activities_description: Plan for activities such as movies, concerts, weekend plans, weeknight hangs, or going out with friends. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.
personal_social.hobbies_description: Costs related to personal interests—like creative supplies, games, or music lessons. Enter how much you expect to spend each month.

other_expenses.title: Other
other_expenses.other_description: Add anything not already covered above. Enter the total amount you expect to spend.

step4_content: Finally, let’s look at the money you’ll have to help cover your costs. Add anything you expect to receive—like support from family, savings, scholarships, or part-time income. Enter all values in Canadian dollars (CAD).

support.support_description: Money you’ll receive up front or regularly from family to help with costs. Enter the total amount you expect to receive.

savings.savings_label: Savings at the start of term
savings.savings_description: Any money you’ve saved before starting school (from work, gifts, etc.). Enter the total amount you expect to contribute.

scholarships.scholarships_description: Money you’ve been awarded—not loaned. Explore UBC’s scholarship opportunities. Enter the total amount you expect to receive in your first year.

earnings.earnings_label: Expected earnings during the study period from a job
earnings.earnings_description: Income you expect to earn during the school year from a part-time job. Enter the total amount you expect to earn.

loans.loans_description: Funding you’ve received from government, bank loans, or community organizations. Enter the total amount you expect to receive.

other_resources.other_resources_description: Any additional financial support you expect to receive to support your education. Enter the total amount you expect to contribute.

step5_title: Total and breakdown of first-year costs
step5_content: You’ve mapped out your costs and expenses—here’s what your first school year could add up to.

grand_total.breakdown_note: Take a look at how your money is split across things like housing, food, and fees below in our cost breakdown.

breakdown_educational.title: Educational costs
breakdown_educational.description: Based on a full first-year 30-credit course load in your chosen program.
breakdown_educational.summary: Tuition is based on a full first-year course load. Most UBC bachelor’s degrees take four years of full-time study to complete. Tuition fees are reviewed annually by the Board of Governors, in consultation with students. In recent years, tuition increases have been 2% for continuing domestic students and between 2% and 5% for continuing international students.

breakdown_core_expenses.title: Living expenses
breakdown_core_expenses.description: These are your estimated living costs—like rent, groceries, and transportation—added up over 8 months.

breakdown_lifestyle_expenses.title: Well-being and lifestyle expenses
breakdown_lifestyle_expenses.description: These are your estimated well-being and lifestyle expenses added up over 8 months

breakdown_financial_support.title: Financial support and resources
breakdown_financial_support.description: This is the total amount of financial support you expect to have over the school year.
